From: Dana Alvarez <dana@medisure.com>

Cc: 
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Log retention attestation + short TTL exception request for forensics

Hi Tessa / Marissa,

As part of our incoming SIG assessment audit (evidence bundle due end of month), Veracity has flagged a gap: MediSure needs a customer-facing attestation that certain API request/response logs will be retained for 90 days for security forensics. Our security team has a firm requirement to preserve request-level logs (headers + timestamps + request id) for 90 days; your public docs show a 30-day default TTL for debug logs.

Can Redwood provide: 1) a short attestation (PDF) that you can retain these logs for MediSure for 90 days, 2) any SOC 2 artifact that describes log retention controls, and 3) a named point of contact for legal/ops so we can route the DocuSign if needed? Please also flag any data minimization concerns.

Audrey Ng from our auditor (audrey@veracitysecurity.com) is copied for evidence requirements.

Thanks — we need to include this in the SIG spreadsheet by Jan 21.

— Dana
Dana Alvarez
Head of Compliance, MediSure Health
(dana@medisure.com)

Attachments: none
From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Log retention attestation + short TTL exception request for forensics

Hi Dana — thanks for the clear ask. We're able to support a scoped 90-day retention for the specific set of request/response traces you listed (request id, timestamps, request metadata; payloads only as needed and redacted per PII rules).

Quick plan:
- I will prepare a 1-page attestation PDF stating Redwood's commitment to retain the named logs for MediSure for 90 days and the conditions under which we will redact or truncate payloads.
- I'll include SOC 2 mapping sections that reference our logging controls and the auditor summary (SOC2-Attestation-2026.pdf).
- We'll route the attestation via DocuSign for your legal signature.

Two operational notes: we need a customer ticket to formally enable this exception (it creates an ephemeral policy override in our retention engine). The ticket will have limited scope (only MediSure tenant IDs: ms-prod and ms-stage) and automatic rollback after 18 months unless renewed. There is a small monthly storage delta; I'll estimate cost separately.

Can you confirm the tenant IDs and whether you want request bodies retained (full vs. redacted)? Also copying Marissa (CS lead) who will own the ticket.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Customer Security Liaison
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-log-retention-matrix.csv (matrix showing default vs exception fields)

Tessa — thanks, I reviewed the matrix. A couple of internal points before we send the attestation:

- Approvals: need written approval from Security (we have it tentatively from security@redwood.ai via Slack thread; I'll request a brief note in the ticket).
- Scope: we should explicitly exclude PII-containing payloads unless MediSure provides a lawful basis and data processing agreement amendment.
- Billing: recommend we include a line item for incremental storage (estimate ~ $1,200/mo at current rates); Rachel can approve any customer credit exceptions.

Next steps I will: open SUP-1248, attach the matrix, and add Security's approval. I'll draft TTL-exception-approval-note.txt for signatures.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
